What the design system is and how to use it

Short answer

Version 2 is a premium redesign of the desktop mock's look. It keeps the same meanings (amber = waiting on you, green = done, red = failed, blue = running or selected, one colour per model) but uses refined values, layered surfaces and soft shadows, a 4 px spacing grid, Windows 11 variable fonts and its own icon set. Every text colour now passes WCAG contrast. Open design-system/gallery.html to see each of the 45 components on its own, with its variants, states and markup. app-mock.html shows them assembled into the window. S1S2S3

45components, each on its own gallery page
41 × 2colour tokens × light/dark
42line icons drawn for the system
37 / 37contrast pairs pass, both themes
  1. One source of values. tokens.json holds every colour, font, spacing, radius, shadow, size and duration. python build_tokens.py writes tokens.css (for the CSS) and tokens.js (for pages opened from file://). S1 VERIFIED
  2. Contrast is checked, not hoped for. build_tokens.py --contrast checks 37 foreground/background pairs in both themes and exits 1 if any falls short. On 2026-11-18 it reported 0 failures. S4 VERIFIED
  3. Components carry their states. Every interactive part has hover, focus, pressed and disabled styles. Matching .is-* classes let the gallery show each state on its own. S2
  4. Each colour role has a text variant. Every status and model colour has a solid, a -soft fill and a -text colour for words on that fill. v1 put status text directly on its soft fill and fell below 4.5:1. S1
  5. It does not depend on the UI stack. The Host stack is decided (D10: Go + Wails), so the WebView links the CSS directly; tokens.json stays the source for generated tokens. S5

Files, and how to preview them

Everything is in harness/kaneki-harness/app/design-system/. Open the HTML files straight from disk; they need no server and no network.

Commands
cd harness/kaneki-harness/app/design-system
python build_tokens.py              # tokens.json → tokens.css + tokens.js
python build_tokens.py --check      # exit 1 if either is out of date
python build_tokens.py --contrast   # WCAG ratio of every listed pair, both themes
start gallery.html                  # Windows: open the component gallery
start app-mock.html                 # the assembled window

The component gallery

The gallery is where each component is designed and reviewed before it goes into a screen. Every example is real markup styled only by components.css, so what you see is what the app will get. S3

The assembled window

app-mock.html builds the main window from the gallery components: ticket rail, pipeline, node card, inspector, sessions dock and live decision log. Rendered by headless Edge at 2× on 2026-11-18.

Colour: roles and values

Each colour is a role, so you pick by meaning, not by hue. Each status and model colour comes in three parts: a solid for marks, a -soft fill, and a -text colour for words on surfaces or on that fill.

Rules for colour

  1. warn means waiting on you, and nothing else. Something waiting shows in the top-bar pill, on the ticket row, as a pipeline node, in a banner, on the session row and in a toast. Nothing else is amber.
  2. Words go in -text, marks go in the solid. PASS is ok-text; the done ring is ok. Every state also has a word or an icon, so colour is never the only signal.
  3. run and accent share a value but mean different things: work in progress versus selection and the primary action.
  4. Model colours appear only on tier badges and cost bars. A badge reads routine · sonnet: the tier first, then the model the profile maps it to. S6

Type, spacing, radius, elevation and motion

Type

display 28/600 · heading 20/600 · title 15/600 (Segoe UI Variable Display)
body-lg 14 · body 13 · body-strong 13/600 · small 12 · caption 11/500 · overline 11/600 uppercase (Segoe UI Variable Text)
code 12 (Cascadia Mono). Numbers in columns use tabular figures.

Spacing

A 4 px grid: space-1 4 · space-2 8 · space-3 12 · space-4 16 · space-5 20 · space-6 24 · space-8 32, with half steps 2, 6 and 10 px for tight controls. Controls are 26, 32 or 38 px tall.

Radius

radius-xs 4 (badges) · radius-sm 6 (buttons, inputs) · radius-md 8 (rows, banners) · radius-lg 12 (cards) · radius-xl 14 (dialogs) · radius-full (pills). The further a layer floats, the softer its corners.

Elevation and motion

Four shadows (xs controls, sm cards, md menus and toasts, lg dialogs) plus focus-ring. In dark mode each shadow adds a faint light edge. Motion: 120 ms responses, 180 ms entries, 260 ms dialogs, one easing curve, and none at all under reduced motion.

Every value above is a token in tokens.json. The gallery's foundation pages show each one with its usage note. S1S3

Changed from v1v1 kept the mock's exact values and generic class names (.btn, .card). v2 renames everything to .k-, replaces emoji and Unicode glyphs (⚙ ▶ ●) with drawn icons, swaps the blue-to-violet gradient logo for a solid ink mark with the pipeline icon, and adds the states, inputs, menus, tooltips, empty states and skeletons the mock did not have. S2S7

Rules for building screens

  1. Every state change shows its command first. A button that runs sdlc gate, invalidate or lane opens a confirmation containing a .k-command block with the exact command line. The app never writes ticket files itself (D1, D2). S5
  2. One primary button per view, named with a verb and its object. The attention button only answers something waiting on the user.
  3. Never colour alone. Pipeline nodes have an icon for each state, verdicts carry their word, and dots carry a label.
  4. Long text goes to Zed. The inspector previews a file with Open in Zed next to it; there is no editing in the app (D9). S5
  5. Build new parts in the gallery first. Add the component to gallery-data.js, check it in light, dark and every state, then use it in a screen.
